claim.claim-text: The claims defining the invention are as follows:
1. A medical record management system administrator comprising:

(a) a data receiver to selectively receive one or more medical files pertaining to a first patient, each file represented in a medical scripting language having, predetermined syntactical and semantic constructs;
(b) a recorder to record and store each medical file of the patient in terms of the predetermined syntactical and semantic constructs; and

(c) a query module to receive a query from a predefined source which has been assigned selective access to the recorded material in terms of the predetermined syntactical and semantic constructs, and to transmit relevant recorded material to that source.

2. The administrator of claim 1 further comprising a pre-emptive report generator to interrogate each medical file and cause predetermined action to take place according to preselected criteria. 3. The administrator of either claims 1 or 2 further comprising a computer upon which the data receiver, recorder and query module, and optionally the report generator is installed.
4. A computerised medical record management system comprising:

(A) an administrator comprising: (a) a data receiver to selectively receive one or more medical files pertaining to a first patient, each file represented in a medical scripting language having predetermined syntactical and semantic constructs;
(b) a recorder to record and store each medical file of the patient in terms of the predetermined syntactical and semantic constructs; and

(c) a query module to receive a query from a predefined source which has been assigned selective access to the recorded material in terms of the predetermined syntactical and semantic constructs, and to transmit relevant recorded material to that source;
(B) a browser to issue search query commands to the query module and to receive and transmit the outcome of the query module to a predetermined source; and
(C) a data input/output screen to input one or more medical files pertaining to the first patient to the data receiver and to receive from the browser, the transmitted outcome of the query module.

5. The system of claim 4 wherein the administrator further comprising a pre-emptive report generator to interrogate each medical file and cause predetermined action to take place according to preselected criteria. 6. The system of either claim 4 or 5 wherein the browser includes a text based editor, standard Mosaic derived internet browsers, and/or a knowledge based medical spreadsheet operating either in or outside the context of an internet browser.

7. A method for medical record management system administration comprising the steps of: (a) selectively receiving one or more medical files pertaining to a first patient, each file represented in a medical scripting language having predetermined syntactical and semantic constructs;

(b) recording and storing each medical file of the patient in terms of the predetermined syntactical and semantic constructs; and (c) processing at least one query from a predefined source which has been assigned selective access to the recorded material, and transmitting the relevant recorded material to that source.

8. The method of claim 7 further comprising the step of interrogating each medical file with a pre-emptive report generator to cause predetermined action to take place according to preselected criteria.

9. The administrator, system and/or method of any of the preceding claims wherein the medical scripting language having predetermined syntactical and semantic constructs, is a high level computer language which represents all aspects of the
health status of a patient including all his attendant past, present and future diagnostic and management issues.

10. The administrator, system and/or method of claim 9, wherein the medical scripting language is characterised by: a) being defined in Extended Backus Naur Format; b) all but natural language style, suitable for human readability and human check on veracity; c) programmable commands. d) being machine interpretable with means for execution of embedded commands; e) being machine interpretable for precision data representation and storage; f) being computer keyword rich; g) constructing patient data into events and placing these events into categories of presentation (symptoms and signs), links (test results), unity (well defined diagnoses) and management (tests and medications), administration, commands, actions and images and denoting each of these categories using keywords; h) being parsable to allow interplay with medical data of the first patient held in the various categories therein; and i) being capable of interacting with a knowledge spreadsheet.

11. The administrator, system and/or method of claim 9, wherein the medical scripting language is a character string in ASCII format or ISO Latin- 1 subset of the Unicode character set or the Unicode character set itself.

12. The administrator, system and/or method of claim 9, wherein the medical scripting language comprises computer keywords which are linnean medical words derived from a linnean classification of all medical objects into species, derived from the steps of :
(a) nominating a linnean medical word as the primary key for each medical object;

(b) classifying each species into the taxa of phylum, class, order, family and genus; (c) using a plurality of alphabetic keys to point to each medical object; classifying the type of alphabetic keys into primary, secondary and tertiary keys;

(d) using an algorithm to generate the secondary key from the primary key that is the linnean medical word; (e) creating a plurality of primary alphabetic keys by using operators to join basic word building blocks to form complex expressions; and

(f) establishing interrelationships among all the species and subspecies medical keywords belonging to the different taxa at the various levels to avoid ambiguity of ostension. 13. The administrator, system and/or method of claim 9, wherein the medical scripting language comprises an event construct including the characteristics of:
(a) each event having the components of
(i) a date/time header,
(ii) a linnean medical word that is humanly readable and defined for the computer interpreter,
(iii) a comment field,
(iv) a field for recording the signature of the person making the entry or amendment,
(v) recordal means for accession details, and (vi) a field to denote the status of the event;

(b) a linnean medical word descriptor describes a presentation, or links or unity or management or administrative data or a command;
wherein the event is the smallest component of data that can effect change in clinical behaviour and the status of each event is denoted as a neutral log event or global active event or global inactive event or negative event to be archived or culled. 14. The administrator, system and/or method of claim 9, wherein the medical scripting language is classified into medical entities including:

(i) symptoms, signs, diagnoses, treatment investigations and investigation results, represented in a linnean hierarchy, and each entity has an alphabetic keyword mapping to a computer object; and (ii) either a presentation type for symptom or sign, a link type for investigation result, a unity type for diagnosis, a management type for drug treatment, an administration type for housekeeping and/or a command type for use in invoking protocols in the supervisory program.

15. The administrator, system and or method of claim 13, wherein the medical scripting language is further characterised by having the events aggregated for administrative, command, action, presentation, links, unity and management items sorted in a chronological order.

16. The administrator, system and/or method of claim 13, wherein the medical scripting language comprises means to represent a snapshot of the present and past patient medical status, comprising all relevant and significant medical information comprising all preventive protocols, and a trace of all events arising from these protocols are held in one location as a file or record.

17. The administrator, system and/or method of claim 13, wherein the medical scripting language comprises the steps of aggregating events into not yet defined entities, about to be defined entities, well defined entities and management, providing the basis for medical problem solving utilising the spreadsheet based process.

18. The administrator, system and/or method of claim 9 wherein the medical scripting language comprises means for embedded commands to do reminders and recall, including the implemented steps of;
(i) establishing a framework for recall starting from three ordered collections of command, action and management;

(ii) allowing the supervisory program to evaluate events in the command collection against the action collection; and (iii) starting from evaluation of events in this framework the step of recall/preventive/administrative action is initiated.

19. The administrator, system and/or method of claim 9 wherein the medical scripting language comprises means for patient privacy protection with implemented steps of: (i) selectively editing patient information capable of identifying the patient to ensure privacy of medical record; and
(ii) assigning an encrypted lock to the edited patient information such that access is only granted by input of a matching encrypted lock.

20. The administrator, system and/or method of claim 9 wherein the scripting language comprises means to preserve the integrity of patient medical files in the event of deprecation of a computer keyword (linnean medical word), including following steps of using a keyword shape change tolerant algorithm:
(i) deprecated linnean words are reassigned as a tertiary key in the computer belief system; (ii) deprecated linnean words are never used again as primary keys;
(iii) deprecated linnean words carry the stigmata of having the @ character in front; and

(iv) on lookup, if a linnean word is missing from the belief system, revision to a stigmatised form is conducted and the lookup is as a tertiary key. 21 The administrator, system and/or method of claims 9 to 20 wherein the medical scripting language with implemented steps of mixing data elements and embedded programming instruction elements into a patient file allows modifications of the embedded commands regarding the patient via a browser.

22. The administrator, system and/or method of claims 9 to 21 wherein the medical scripting language, comprises means for rewriting itself into a new program with new embedded behaviour; with the implemented steps of :
(i) the execution of embedded commands based on the relationship among the command/action/management triad of collections;
(ii) leading to health care action or notification of patient/healthcare worker;
(iii) the automatic generation of an action event ;
(iv) the logging of this action event in the action collection;

(v) the writing out of the changed patient medical scripting language file; with resultant changed behaviour of the altered patient file itself next time around, after any embedded command has been triggered.

23. The administrator, system and/or method of claims 9 to 22 wherein the medical scripting language, comprising means for cognating two separate files of the same patient into a single file to comprise all the data held in both files by the implemented steps of :
(i) reading in the first file;
(ii) deconstructing events into their various collections;
(iii) reading the second file;
(iv) deconstructing events into their various collections; and (v) merging the two disparate collections and establishing the new file.

24. The administrator, system and/or method of claims 9 to 22 wherein the medical scripting language includes a round trip inter-conversion from its original format to hypertext markup language (HTML) or any derivative of standard generalised markup language (SGML), and back to the original medical scripting language. 25. The method of claim 7 wherein the transmission of the outcome of the query is to a medical spreadsheet browser and the query is complied by the steps of:
(i) requesting patient file written from the administrator;

(ii) opening and parsing each patient file;
(iii) extracting all commands to be executed embedded in the patient file ;
(iv) storing all presentation or symptoms or signs events in a data collection and displaying them on a computer pane;
(v) storing all links or medical investigation result events in a data collection and displaying them on a computer pane;
(vi) storing all unity or diagnosis events in a data collection;
(vii) storing all management or prescription or procedure events in a data collection and displaying them on a computer pane;
(viii) developing possible solutions within a framework of an interrelationship among preselected medical data; and
(ix) scrolling and saving worksheets.
26. The method of claim 7 wherein the query outcome is downloaded in HTML format to be viewed as a web page with a Mosaic type browser.
27. The method of claim 7 wherein the query outcome is downloaded in ASCII character string format to be viewed as a document by a text editor.
